hints: Look closely at X on the right side of the cell. Notice it is a stack of membranes around the nucleus and it is covered in tiny black dots.
Remember what those tiny dots are, and remember that the folded membranes form tubes and sacs (cisternae) that can carry substances away.
walkthrough:
**Identify structure X**

Look at the drawing. X points to flattened membrane sacs arranged in parallel stacks, continuous with the nuclear envelope.

Crucially, the outer surface is studded with tiny dots. Those dots are ribosomes.

**Link structure to function**

Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis. So a membrane covered in ribosomes must be involved in making proteins.

The membranes form enclosed channels called cisternae. Newly made proteins enter these channels and are transported in vesicles to the Golgi body and beyond.

**Choose the complete function**

X is the rough endoplasmic reticulum. It does two linked jobs, it makes proteins (on its ribosomes) and it transports them (inside its membranes).

That matches protein synthesis and transport.

options.A: Lipid synthesis is the main role of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, which has no ribosomes. X is rough because it has ribosomes.
options.B: X is rough endoplasmic reticulum. Its ribosomes synthesise proteins and its cisternae transport them to the Golgi in vesicles.
options.C: Protein synthesis does happen on the ribosomes of X, but this is incomplete because the membrane system also transports the proteins.
options.D: Protein transport does happen inside X, but this is incomplete because the attached ribosomes also synthesise the proteins.
